title: A protocol for preparation and transfection of rat entorhinal cortex organotypic cultures for electrophysiological whole-cell recordings
author: Cilz, Porter, et al.

steps.title: Fix slices for immunostaining
steps.instruction: Immerse cultured entorhinal cortex slices in 4 % paraformaldehyde solution for 24 h at room temperature.

steps.title: Mount slices on microscope slides
steps.instruction: After fixation, transfer each slice individually onto frosted microscope slides (VWR catalog #12‑550‑15).

steps.title: Immunostain for neuronal marker NeuN
steps.instruction: Perform immunofluorescent staining using the NeuN primary antibody (Milipore, catalog #ABN78) at a 1:200 dilution, following the adapted protocol from reference [2].

steps.title: Assess slice health electrophysiologically
steps.instruction: Using high‑magnification differential interference contrast (DIC) microscopy, locate healthy principal neurons (e.g., layer II at DIV 4). Apply direct positive current steps to elicit graded action potentials and negative current steps to observe early sag responses; record input‑output curves to confirm excitability comparable to acute p16 slices.

steps.title: Prepare DNA cartridge for biolistic transfection
steps.instruction: Mix plasmid DNA constructs at the desired ratio: for co‑expression use a 1:1 ratio (25 µg of each plasmid) added to the gold‑particle cartridge; for a reporter‑only condition adjust to a 0.75:0.25 gene‑of‑interest : reporter ratio.

steps.title: Biolistically transfect slices on DIV 2
steps.instruction: At 2 days in vitro (DIV 2), deliver the DNA‑coated gold particles to the slices using a biolistic gene‑gun; ensure slices have adhered to the membrane before the pressure burst to avoid loss.

steps.title: Incubate and record post‑transfection
steps.instruction: Maintain transfected slices in culture and perform whole‑cell recordings 36–72 h after transfection (i.e., between DIV 3.5 and DIV 5), confirming GFP (or RFP) expression and normal electrophysiological properties.
